question_text: Draw the graph of y = tan x on (−π/2, π/2).

recall_prompt: Say how you would draw this one — name the values you plot, what happens at the two ends, and the shape you get.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Table of values and the asymptotes
steps.margin_note: First mark. Five easy values fix the middle of the curve and the two limits fix the ends. tan 0 = 0, so the curve passes through the origin.
steps.memory_tip: Plot five easy values, then the two ends: tan x falls without limit near −π/2 and rises without limit near π/2.
lines: y = tan x is defined for every x in (−π/2, π/2).
As x nears −π/2 from the right, tan x → −∞.
As x nears π/2 from the left, tan x → +∞.
So x = −π/2 and x = π/2 are asymptotes.

recall.must_convey: That tan(±π/4) = ±1, tan(±π/3) = ±√3 and tan 0 = 0 are used, and that tan x goes to −∞ near −π/2 and to +∞ near π/2, so x = ±π/2 are asymptotes.
accept: tan of pi by four is one and tan of pi by three is root three and tan zero is zero
near minus pi by two the value goes to minus infinity and near pi by two to plus infinity
the lines x equals plus and minus pi by two are asymptotes
rendu chivarla asymptotes untai, x equals plus minus pi by two
make a small table of values and note the two asymptotes

steps.why: The interval is open, so the two ends are never reached. Naming them as asymptotes is what tells the reader that the curve keeps rising and never touches those lines.
common_mistakes: Joining the two ends of the curve across x = π/2, which would make one continuous line.
Drawing the curve as if it stopped at a finite height at each end.

steps.label: Draw the graph
steps.margin_note: Second mark, and the point of the question. Draw the axes first, then the two dashed asymptotes, then one single curve between them, rising all the way and passing through the origin.
steps.memory_tip: One branch only, rising from bottom left to top right through the origin, held between the two dashed lines.

recall.must_convey: That the axes are drawn, the asymptotes x = ±π/2 marked as dashed lines, and one increasing branch of y = tan x drawn between them through the origin. Naming the drawing is full credit.
accept: draw the axes, mark the two dashed asymptotes and draw one rising branch through the origin
sketch one branch of tan x between x equals minus pi by two and pi by two
draw the curve going from bottom left up to top right through O
axes geesi, rendu dashed lines geesi, madhyalo okka branch geeyali
draw the graph with the two asymptotes shown

steps.why: On this interval y = tan x is ONE branch, not several. Drawing the dashed lines first keeps that branch inside them, which is what stops the usual mistake of joining neighbouring branches into a wave.
common_mistakes: Drawing a repeating wave, which is the shape of sin x and not of tan x.
Letting the curve touch or cross an asymptote.
Drawing the curve falling instead of rising — tan x increases across the whole interval.
